name: which
description: Shows the full path of an executable that the shell would run.

flags.description: Path of the first matching executable in $PATH.
Show ALL matches in PATH order.
Behave as if PATH were the default.

examples.explanation: The python3 that will actually run.
Two node installations exist; the first in PATH wins. Classic cause of "wrong version running".
Empty output means the command is not in PATH — not installed, or PATH is incomplete (common in cron).

about: which searches $PATH only. It cannot see aliases, functions, or builtins — use type for the complete picture. In scripts, command -v NAME is the POSIX-portable existence check.
useCases: Find where a program is installed.
Verify a command exists before calling it.
mistakes: Using which in scripts for existence checks — command -v is portable and builtin.
